source.title: Every Ablation Is a Dose: Counterweights and the Semblance of Self-Repair
source.authors: Areeb Ahmad; Pratinav Seth; Vinay Kumar Sankarapu

page_placements.theme: Refinements and look-alikes of the copy-suppression mechanism
Named sources of compensation other than copy suppression, and how large they are

record.tranche_reason: The paper uses a dose-graded causal intervention and a downstream contribution measure to test self-repair and the role of GPT-2 Small L10.h7 in IOI. This is a conceptual test, not the original copy-suppression measurement.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a GPT-2 Small IOI dose-response for L10.h7 and other heads, plus a final-normalization audit on three factual-verdict models. It does not measure earlier-token copying, token-logit suppression from copying, calibration, or the head's share of loss. The IOI head-weight correlations and dose placements are not direct measurements of the copy-suppression behavior in V1 or the loss share in V2.
record.test_reason: In GPT-2 Small IOI, the study dose-swaps the upstream name-mover core (L9.h6+L9.h9). It measures how the copy-suppression head L10.h7's contribution to the name margin changes. Its opposition shrinks as the core's signal is removed. This bears on V4 (copy suppression as a self-repair mechanism) using a different, dose-graded method. It does not measure copy-suppression behaviour itself, loss share, calibration, or distribution-wide self-repair.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors argue that self-repair is the release of a standing, affine coupling already present in the clean model, not a reactive recruitment. In GPT-2 IOI, all seven law-following reachable heads are counterweights, with the copy-suppression head L10.h7 dominant. The ≤4.5% renormalization bound applies to their dosed-swap recruitment in the factual models. They state that deletion-type interventions do involve the LayerNorm mediator.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses nested, dose-graded core swaps and regime-matched downstream activation patching, rather than the original copy-suppression analysis. It measures changes in head contribution to an IOI name margin, not copied-token logits or loss.
record.method_sensitivity: For L11.h10, including L10.h7 in the clamped core changes the response from curved to nearly affine and increases the fitted coupling. The paper also notes that a second reference convention gives different certifications and looser held-out prediction, while qualitative conclusions hold.

fits_no_version.finding: Several IOI backup and name-mover heads are certified counterweights to the name-mover core in the clean model, with γ from −0.127 to −0.018.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In GPT-2 Small IOI, backup heads oppose the name-mover core in the clean model, and ablation releases a standing coupling.

fits_no_version.finding: L11.h10's curved response becomes affine once L10.h7 is clamped into the core. L10.h7 mediates the other negative name mover.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The two IOI negative name movers compose: L11.h10's response to the core is mediated by L10.h7.

fits_no_version.finding: Final-norm rescaling accounts for at most 4.5% of recruitment under a dosed swap in three 7–9B instruct models on a factual task.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under class-swap interventions, LayerNorm rescaling contributes little to compensatory recruitment.

record.code_released: not stated; code and per-run outputs are promised for the camera-ready version
record.problems: The GPT-2 Small arm is one model on one task with a small head set (10 reachable heads). The authors note that held-out dose tests interpolate rather than extrapolate and do not select the affine law over smooth alternatives. The paper does not test classic copy-suppression behavior, calibration, or loss attribution.
record.rows_left_out: Other GPT-2 Small head responses and detailed held-out-dose values are not separately cataloged where they do not change the reported claim-relevant results. Factual-task counterweight tables beyond the selected renormalization audit are omitted because they concern other directions rather than L10.h7 or copy-suppression behavior.

untested.parts: Whether L10.h7 attends to earlier predicted tokens and suppresses their logits across the training distribution.
The QK/OV copy-suppression mechanism and its share of the head's loss effect. The §L.4 Q-composition correlation concerns coupling to the core, not V2.
Whether L10.h7's released opposition is copy suppression specifically. Self-repair outside IOI. Deletion-style ablation rather than the dosed swap.
Whether IOI negative name movers or heads in other models are copy suppression. Role labels are taken from prior work.
The share of self-repair attributable to copy suppression versus other mechanisms across the training distribution.

missing.what: Under the alternative reference convention, all ten reachable heads certify and held-out prediction is looser (median |z| 0.41). This bears on the robustness of r1 and r8.
The only held-out points beyond 2 SE are L10.h7 at λ=−½. L10.h7 is strongly curved inside the window.

record.verdict_notes: Only r1 bears on a version (V4). The record's V5 and V6 labels are dropped. IOI head labels come from Wang et al. and McDougall et al., and the factual-model rows do not involve copy suppression. The study cites McDougall et al. but is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Whether L10.h7 attends to earlier occurrences of predicted tokens and lowers their logits, especially across the training distribution.
The specified QK/OV copy-suppression circuit and whether it explains 76.9% of the head's effect on loss.
Calibration and overconfidence in naive copying.

The study tests compensation after dosing upstream IOI name-mover heads, but does not test self-repair across tasks or show the fraction of ordinary self-repair attributable specifically to copy suppression.
The study examines L10.h7 and other IOI heads, but does not test the classic earlier-token copying behavior, other negative name movers beyond the reported circuit, or other model sizes.

The study audits final-normalization rescaling and reports counterweight responses, but does not apportion all self-repair across all possible mechanisms or establish the claim across the training distribution.

rows.operation_detail: Dosed-swap the L9.h6 + L9.h9 name-mover core and measure L10.h7's regime-consistent counterfactual contribution; fit a shared slope on the on-manifold dose window.
rows.measure: On-manifold coupling slope γr for L10.h7
rows.note: L10.h7 is identified as the copy-suppression head and a negative name mover. The paper reports this as the largest coupling among the reachable heads: seven times the next largest and twenty times the median.
rows.check: Linked only to V4. The study takes the head's role labels from prior work and does not test whether IOI negative name movers are copy suppression (V5). IOI is not the training distribution, so the row cannot speak to V6's distribution-wide share.

relation.reason: The study reports its own causal measurements of L10.h7's response to intervention on upstream name movers.

tranche.reason: Dose-graded core swaps and nested downstream interventions measure the release of L10.h7's opposition when upstream name-mover signal is reduced, using a different method to address the V4 compensation question.

source_check.notes: Copy-suppression self-repair evidence is confined to GPT-2 Small IOI; the factual-task normalization audit does not establish V6 or transfer to deletion interventions. Preserve the source's distinct L11.h10 fits: Table 31 gives γr = −0.0348, Figure 29 gives −0.0701; Figure 26 reports a curvature ratio of 3.430 versus 2.608 in §L.3.

statements.correction: §L.2: L10.h7 certifies; the only two held-out class means beyond 2 SE are its λ = −½ points. §L.3: L11.h10 is the affine-law exception, with R² = 0.413 and |βr/γr| = 2.608 under the two-head core; L10.h7 is described as strongly curved. §L.6: all ten reachable heads certify under the alternative reference convention; median |z| = 0.41; qualitative conclusions hold under both conventions.
statements.problem: The numerical and held-out-test claims match, but identifying L10.h7 as the least linear head conflicts with the reported L11.h10 exception. No numerical comparison of L10.h7 slopes across reference conventions is supplied.
